what: Confirmed vs. suspected: the branch-prefix signal
title: Measuring AI involvement in a repository: the epiworld case
text: Coding agents push prefixed branches, prefix often longest-lived trace AI involvement: survives squash-merges shows even bot account commit trailer . gh_pulls() returns head branch, ai_classify() reads : two tiers real work . Every copilot/* pull request opened Copilot bot account, confirmed via identity. codex/* ones look similar opened human: exactly branch prefix recorded ai_suspected rather folded ai. Agents open pull requests leave pattern: developer runs agent locally, pushes branch produced, opens PR account. prefix says AI probably involved; say wrote line, principle human name branch copilot/... agent involved . Read ai lower bound AI involvement ai | ai_suspected upper bound:
code: data(epiworld_pulls)  pulls <- ai_classify(epiworld_pulls, patterns = ai_only)  pulls[, .N, by = .(ai, ai_suspected, ai_evidence, ai_agent)] #>        ai ai_suspected ai_evidence ai_agent     N #>    <lgcl>       <lgcl>      <char>   <char> <int> #> 1:  FALSE        FALSE        <NA>     <NA>    98 #> 2:   TRUE        FALSE    identity  copilot    54 #> 3:  FALSE         TRUE      branch   openai     2 pulls[ai_suspected == TRUE, .(number, user, branch, ai_agent, ai_evidence)] #>    number     user                              branch ai_agent ai_evidence #>     <int>   <char>                              <char>   <char>      <char> #> 1:    232 gvegayon         codex/switch-docs-to-mrdocs   openai      branch #> 2:    237 gvegayon codex/poisson-default-using-le-cams   openai      branch pulls[, .(   pull_requests = .N,   confirmed     = sum(ai),   upper_bound   = sum(ai | ai_suspected) )] #>    pull_requests confirmed upper_bound #>            <int>     <int>       <int> #> 1:           154        54          56

title: Measuring AI involvement in a repository: the epiworld case
text: ai_classify() deliberately parsimonious: catches AI involvement visible (bot identities, attribution trailers, mentions). Undisclosed AI assistance–e.g., code written editor completions committed human identity–detectable API metadata alone, figures lower bounds. Net lines changed rough proxy project size; includes documentation data files unless filtered (use file-level output gh_commit_lines() ). gh_traffic() (clones/views) covers last 14 days requires push access, building long download history requires periodic snapshots.

what: Measure the Effects of AI Coding Using the GitHub API
title: Measure the Effects of AI Coding Using the GitHub API
text: aitracking lightweight R pipeline measure effects AI-assisted coding software projects using GitHub REST API. retrieves commit histories (lines added/deleted), issue pull request conversations, download/clone statistics, evolution project’s size; classifies events involved AI coding agent; visualizes result. Design goals: Minimal dependencies. GitHub API client written base R connections; hard dependencies data.table jsonlite. Pipe-friendly. Every function takes data first argument returns data.table, steps compose R’s native pipe |>. Parsimonious AI detection. small, transparent set rules (author/committer identities, Co-authored-:/Generated trailers, @-mentions) flags AI involvement. Extend patterns.

title: Measure the Effects of AI Coding Using the GitHub API
text: single field GitHub API says “AI wrote ”, ai_classify() combines traces projects agents actually leave, reports two tiers: Confirmed (ai == TRUE) Agent identities author, committer, assignee, commenter fields (Copilot, devin-ai-integration[bot], cursoragent, …). Note GitHub’s coding agent appears login Copilot type Bot without [bot] suffix, agents plain User accounts – neither suffix account type sufficient . Attribution trailers commit messages PR/issue bodies: Co-authored-: (Copilot, Claude, Cursor emit default), Assisted-: convention projects prefer marks assistance without implying co-authorship. Suspected (ai_suspected == TRUE) Agent branch prefixes copilot/fix-thing codex/add-tests. longest-lived trace – survives squash-merges – weaker evidence, human may create branch agent’s behalf: several agents open pull requests , developer runs agent locally, pushes branch, opens PR account. Treat ai lower bound ai | ai_suspected upper bound. Separately, ai_mention flags text addresses agent (@copilot fix ), proxy much humans prompting AI. Undisclosed assistance – code written editor completions committed human identity trailer – detectable API metadata . Every figure package produces therefore lower bound.

title: Classify AI involvement in commits and interactions — ai_classify
text: copy x data.table new columns: ai: logical, TRUE confirmed involvement, .e., AI account authored/committed/assigned row (identity), text carries attribution trailer naming agent (trailer). ai_suspected: logical, TRUE suspected involvement, .e., evidence agent branch prefix (see Details). Confirmed suspected mutually exclusive: row ai never ai_suspected. ai_agent: label matching agent (NA neither flag set). ai_evidence: triggered flag—"identity", "trailer", "branch"—classification can audited tier dropped. ai_mention: (text columns present) label AI agent mentioned/addressed text (e.g., "@copilot fix "), NA otherwise. Rows !ai & !.na(ai_mention) proxy humans prompting AI agents.

title: aitracking (development version)
text: New gh_assignments(): issues pull requests together accounts assigned , flagging ones delegated AI coding agent (assigned_ai, assigned_agent). Assigning issue Copilot coding agent given task, rows measure delegation AI rather AI involvement resulting code. New gh_pulls(): pull requests including head branch name. New gh_copilot_metrics() gh_copilot_seats(): organization-level Copilot usage. Note usage metrics require organization ownership “Copilot usage metrics” policy; public per-repository endpoint, endpoint exposes tokens hours spent. ai_classify() now reports evidence two tiers. ai stays confirmed involvement (agent identity, attribution trailer); new ai_suspected marks suspected involvement, currently agent branch prefixes copilot/... codex/.... branch prefix weaker evidence human may create branch agent’s behalf. new ai_evidence column records rule fired ("identity"/"trailer"/"branch"), assignee branch columns now scanned default. ai_classify() recognizes Assisted-: trailer alongside Co-authored-: Generated . ai_patterns() gained jules coderabbit, split Jules gemini pattern. plot_timeline() draws suspected AI involvement band, confirmed count never inflated . Failed API requests now report HTTP status likely cause (bad token, exhausted rate limit, missing scope, org policy) instead generic connection error. New example datasets epiworld_assignments epiworld_pulls.

title: aitracking 0.1.0
text: GitHub REST API access base R connections (gh_api(), gh_token()). Commit history retrieval per-commit line counts (gh_commits(), gh_commit_lines()). Traffic, release-download, interaction, language retrieval (gh_traffic(), gh_downloads(), gh_interactions(), gh_languages()). Rule-based AI-involvement classification (ai_classify(), ai_patterns()). Project size evolution (loc_evolution()) activity timelines (plot_timeline()). Example datasets UofUEpiBio/epiworld C++ library.
